answer: Call it **arrival-curve fingerprinting**: an agent’s request interarrival times must form a karst-like decay from burst to steady drip, and a new identity gets throttled until its curve matches an established willow profile across several windows. Enforcement compares each identity’s timing distribution to a terrace of historical baselines, flagging synthetic bursts that flatten into uniform polling. An attacker pays roughly 40 hours of organic pacing per identity before earning full throughput, so scaling a sybil fleet multiplies wall-clock time, not just compute.
